Used only when the marker above is set to \"Custom…\". One character; if you enter more, only the first is used. A glyph that can also appear in real text (a check mark, an emoji) becomes indistinguishable from the marker.

Colors for the \"Copy image\" output — background and per-role text (base, furigana, romaji, gloss). Whatever scheme you pick, text is auto-adjusted to stay legible against its background. Plain-text output is unaffected.
Off by default. When enabled, Japanglify starts a low-priority, cancellable image preview after text conversion so Copy image can be faster. Leave off to keep text-only work lean.
Used only when the scheme above is \"Custom…\". Enter a hex color like #RRGGBB. Text is still auto-adjusted for legibility against your background.
Preview — how each format renders "日本語"; the selected one is bold
Controls wrapping in generated images from both Copy image and Share. Default 14 is narrow; use 40–80+ for wider images, or 0 for unlimited.
Preview — actual wrap depends on the host\'s font/size
Vertical (tategaki) is experimental for plain-text hosts
This removes the downloaded %1$s dictionary from this device. You can download it again later.
Show a brief English meaning under each word and particle. Needs a downloaded dictionary above. Experimental — still being refined; off by default.

A word can have several dictionary senses (e.g. すごい: \"terrible\" vs. \"amazing\") — which one gets shown. Modern favors richer, non-dated senses. Classical favors older/archaic ones, for reading dated source text. Custom exposes the underlying weights below.

Max characters shown for a word\'s English gloss before its extra \"/\"-joined synonyms are dropped — a short list that already fits (like さん\'s \"Mr/Mrs/Miss\") is kept in full either way; a long one (like \"do/to carry out/to perform\") trims down. Lower keeps output more compact; higher shows more nuance.
Custom: dated weight (negative penalizes, positive favors)

Show a precise emoji under a word\'s gloss when one exists, e.g. 紙 → paper → 📄. Needs word/particle glosses on above, and the emoji data downloaded here. Experimental — still being refined; off by default.
Normally a precise emoji match replaces its now-redundant English word. Enable to keep both.
Which parts of speech are eligible for an emoji match — default is all, though concrete nouns match far more often than verbs or particles.
Select Japanese text anywhere, tap Japanglify in the selection menu. Editable fields are replaced; read-only selections are copied. Change options here — the menu action never prompts.

Cut/Copy/Paste are the main row — Japanglify is never there. Android only adds PROCESS_TEXT apps under ⋮, and only if the host found any. No ⋮ at all = empty list (host does not query PROCESS_TEXT, or Japanglify is not installed). Fallbacks: Try it button, Clipboard button, or Share → Japanglify. Support varies by app — some show it, others never will.
Why the menu only works inside Japanglify
✓ Our PROCESS_TEXT activity is registered and this app can resolve it
✗ Not resolved — reinstall the APK, then open this screen again
PROCESS_TEXT apps visible to Japanglify: %1$d (including us: %2$d)
Handlers Japanglify can see (because we declare <queries>):\n%1$s

Japanglify is not “hooking” other apps. The host app builds the selection menu. When you select text here, Japanglify is the host, so it can list PROCESS_TEXT activities (including itself). Other apps either never call PROCESS_TEXT, or (Android 11+) cannot see third-party PROCESS_TEXT apps without their own <queries> — we cannot add that for them.

Not a Japanglify registration bug: the APK correctly exports ProcessTextActivity. Other apps choose whether to offer process-text items. If an app never offers it, use Copy assist (Accessibility) instead — selection-menu support varies by app.
Cut/Copy/Paste only + no ⋮ = that host found zero PROCESS_TEXT apps (or never queries them). Use Copy assist or the live field below.
Page text loaded into the field below — edit it down to the part you want, then tap Japanglify

Type or paste Japanese — live output updates below. Buttons convert in place or from the clipboard. Options further down scroll with this page.
Clipboard is empty or not readable (focus this app, copy text, try again)

Restarts the Copy-assist foreground service (if enabled) and refreshes the conversion engine. If Accessibility (the main Copy hook) is off, opens Accessibility settings so you can turn it back on — apps can\'t re-enable it automatically.
Primary path: select text, then tap the Japanglify chip. Requires Accessibility. The older Copy, Cut and Paste hooks are optional fallbacks below.
Required: enable “Japanglify Copy assist”. Copy detection will not work without this.
On — Copy in any app triggers Japanglify
Off — enable this for the Copy hook
Extra clipboard listener with a persistent notification. Prefer Accessibility alone when possible.
Shows the primary in-context action when you select text. Turning it off leaves Share and the fallback controls available.

When you Cut Japanese text in an editable field, replace it in place with the Japanglified version. Separate from Copy (which only shows a result notification). Turn off to leave Cut as an ordinary system cut. Needs Accessibility, same as Copy.
Save current settings as a Share target…
Adds a new icon to the system Share sheet that always converts with today\'s settings, even if you change them later — e.g. a "Romaji only" target for a chat that can\'t show furigana well.
Remove saved targets. To change a target\'s settings, delete it and save a new one with the settings you want.
Enter a name for this target
This device only allows %1$d Share targets. Delete one first.
When you Copy text, Japanglify expands it and notifies you (for apps without a process-text menu)

Primary feature: detect Copy in any app, expand Japanese with furigana/romaji, and show a notification. Tap the notification to copy the result for Paste. Also remembers the current selection so processing works even when Android hides clipboard contents. Optional floating chip on selection. Only selected/copied text is used while enabled; not for advertising.
Notification permission is required so Copy results can be shown.
